title: The Dark Culinary World
text: “Motoyasu-san! You don’t need to go adding unnecessary commentary!”
“A ball that seems to have trouble breathing… could it possibly be—”
“Naofumi-san, please don’t say anything more! That me and the current me are walking down completely different paths of fate, so please don’t worry about it!”
“Setting aside the story of the Bow Hero from the first world, Gaelion thinks it’d be fine to put him in the treasure vault Gaelion made and keep watch over him, nano.”
“Gaelion-san, if it were Naofumi-san you were collecting, sure, but what’s the point of collecting me!”
“Well, I’d really rather you didn’t?”
“There’s no deep meaning behind it, nano. Naofumi, Gaelion may have a hobby of adoring Naofumi, but Gaelion wouldn’t do that sort of thing to a Naofumi who’s unwilling, nano.”
“I have my doubts about the ’adoring’ part too, though.”
“That’s right, Rival! Don’t let it do such a thing!”

Collecting Father, you say? Indeed, across all the countless loops there have been many different Fathers, so in a sense I have collected quite the variety in my memories, I say. There are all sorts of Fathers, after all.

“Gaelion already said it wouldn’t, nano. Oh, but nano, apparently among the past Dragon Emperors there were some real nasty types who’d defeat a hero, absorb them, and keep them alive-but-barely as a power source, nano.”
“Gaelion-san, are you really okay saying that out loud?”

“Even if Gaelion did something like that, it wouldn’t get Gaelion the Naofumi Gaelion wants, and Gaelion couldn’t face anyone afterward, nano. It’d be hollow, nano. Besides, doing that would definitely get other heroes summoned and killed for certain, nano. Threat level would skyrocket, nano.”
“Yeah, that sounds genuinely dangerous. I guess we should be relieved Gaelion-chan has no intention of doing it… she’s harmless, at least in that sense.”
“The sexual harassment toward Naofumi-san has really died down, hasn’t it. We should thank Naofumi-san for taming Gaelion-san.”
“Calling it ’taming’ is rude, nano. Gaelion would like you to say ’came to love,’ nano.”
Guh… Rival! Just how much psychological damage do you intend to inflict on me, I say! Itsuki glanced at me with a look of distaste as I coughed up blood, then turned her gaze to Rival.
“Itsuki, I think it’s best not to worry too much about why Motoyasu-kun is spitting up blood. You’re bound to step on a landmine.”
“Now I’m curious, but fine, I understand. What kind of person was the Naofumi-san who loved Gaelion-san, to Motoyasu-san, I wonder?”
“He is the Father who devoted himself so entirely to me that he sold his own body to Rival, I say! Guhhh…”
“Somehow it feels like Motoyasu-kun has a serious misunderstanding going on.”
“Nano, Gaelion was told to get along with the Spear Hero and guide him well. Gaelion is making an effort to keep that promise, nano.”
Guhhhh… I say!
“So as a result, Gaelion-san ended up like this, and Motoyasu-san became even stranger, is that the gist of it?”
“Hmm… I guess this must be a landmine topic about me for Motoyasu-kun. Probably safest not to talk about it too much.”
“Ahh, Father… The one who staked his very body for my sake and offered it up to Rival, I say.”
I offer a prayer of penance to Father, I say.
“At this point it’s basically a religion.”
“Having someone pray to a me that isn’t me is kind of a weird feeling… If I end up in some other loop, I bet I’ll end up as an object of prayer too.”
“In a sense, you could call Motoyasu-san a devout follower of the Shield Hero faith, perhaps.”
“I wonder about that phrasing? Isn’t he more of a Filolial worshipper?”
“Probably he worships both. The great Filo-san, and her parent, the omniscient and omnipotent god Naofumi-san.”
“Itsuki, you never change. Though it’s true enough that I can’t really argue back.”
So the others were talking amongst themselves while I was busy praying, I say.
“The actual heroes are pretty different from the legends, kyu.”
“Yeah, that’s true. But that doesn’t change the job we have to do. Itsuki-kun! If anything comes up, rely on me. I might not be very dependable, but I’ll do my best!”
“Itsuki, it’s not like that anime, but if you’d properly be Raph-emon’s friend, I’d be happy about it, personally.”
“With this much devotion, I can’t just brush it off. There’s probably a version of me somewhere who would do something like that, but that’s not me.”
“I’ll do what needs doing, until it’s done…”
And so, saying something along those lines, Raph-emon’s renovations came to an end, I say.

Some time after that, I say. For the sake of Panda’s mental stability while pregnant and unsettled, Father decided to take Big Sister and Older Sister, along with some other villagers, and spend some time at Panda’s homeland. On top of that, Father mentioned plans for diplomacy toward Siltvelt and a visit to Elephant’s house as well. Of course, whenever there was time to spare, he’d come back to the village via portal.

Rival went along with Father and the others. At Father’s request, I was left to watch over the village in his absence, I say. I was a bit uneasy, but since Fleon-chan and Filo-ko-chan were also accompanying Father, I felt reassured.
Then, one day, a visitor came to the village, I say. Apparently someone had come via Éclair to make a request to Elephant. Supposedly a merchant that Éclair and Elephant patronized.
“Well, well… um, the Bow Hero and Spear Hero-sama… I’ve heard rumors of you both.”
“Is that so.”
We were treated as the heroes who saved the world from the Waves, I say. That kind of reputation had apparently spread across the whole world.
“Um… is the Shield Hero-sama present, by chance?”
It seemed the business was with Father. Perhaps the merchant was already acquainted with him?
“He’s away right now. To be precise, he’s out on diplomatic business toward Siltvelt.”
“I-I see…”
Whatever could have happened, I wonder?
“What’s your business? I can at least relay a message?”
“Well then… the Shield Hero-sama is, by rumor, quite the skilled cook, I hear.”
“You want to eat Naofumi-san’s cooking?”
“You could say that, or you could say it’s not quite that. To put it briefly, there’s a world of chefs in Zeltoble called the Dark Culinary World…”
The Dark Culinary World, was it? So such a world truly exists.

“What is it? Are you here to scout Naofumi-san into this Dark Culinary World, or perhaps to pick a fight? Come to throw down a challenge to the Shield Hero rumored to cook so well? I don’t think he’ll take you up on it, though.”
“Heavens, no. That’s not it at all. Rather, I’ve come at the direct request of the leadership of the Dark Culinary World, to ask for… reinforcements.”
“I see…”

The merchant’s story went like this, I say. Currently, in the Dark Culinary World rooted in Zeltoble, there was a mysterious chef causing havoc, sweeping through the Dark Cooking Colosseum and defeating chef after chef, leaving everyone in trouble. Whenever this chef appeared, every competitor was utterly and completely crushed, unable to do a thing against them. Some who lost to this chef had apparently gone missing or been socially destroyed. In order to somehow stop this threat rampaging through the Dark Culinary World, the organization was reaching out to chefs with even a modicum of fame in the ordinary world, asking them to serve as reinforcements and enter the Dark Cooking Colosseum where this chef competed.
“A Dark Culinary World and a Dark Cooking Colosseum… Zeltoble really does have everything, doesn’t it.”
“Indeed. And so, word reached the Shield Hero-sama, who has deep connections with the Earthshaking Queen and the Bamboo Grove… and with what’s said to be an equally promising rising star.”
“Is it really alright to invite a hero to a place like that?”
“Naturally, he would participate with his identity concealed.”
“What’s the chance the Dark Culinary World is lying just to lure Naofumi-san out?”

“That would be quite difficult, I should think… As I mentioned, we’re connected to merchants who themselves have ties to famous fighters here in Zeltoble, and lying would give them an opening to exploit—and of course, it risks turning Faubrey and Melromarc against us as well.”
Hmm… it did seem like they were genuinely in trouble and reaching out to Father.
“You want Naofumi-san to defeat this chef in question…”
“Yes. Would you be able to pass along the request?”

“Well, that said… we personally have absolutely no reason to participate, so all I can really say is please come back when he’s actually here… Ah, come to think of it, I believe I heard that Zeltoble has been frowning at Naofumi-san ever since he scouted those three mercenaries.”
“If at all possible, it would be a great help to the leadership of Zeltoble as a whole if he could participate.”

Hmm… Itsuki crossed her arms and groaned. Now then, what to do? At present, I was the one entrusted with matters in Father’s absence, I say. And at the same time, thanks to Rival, my standing had been steadily plummeting. So what would happen if I swooped in and resolved this matter Father had been asked about, all on my own?
“Wow, Motoyasu-kun! You defeated my enemy! Thank you! Gaelion—no, that useless dragon’s got nothing on you, you’re way more helpful!”
“N-nano—!? Naofumi, don’t throw Gaelion away, nano—!”
“Well then, let’s toss the dragon and get along with Motoyasu-kun and the others instead.”
Such a scene unfolded in my mind. This was it, I say! I would carry this out flawlessly in Father’s stead!
“Itsuki, there is absolutely no need for Father to go himself, I say.”
“What is it, Motoyasu-san? Don’t tell me you’re saying there’s no need to trouble Naofumi-san because you’ll physically reduce this chef to ash?”
“Not so, I say. This Motoyasu, while not on Father’s level, has confidence in his own cooking, I say. So I shall go in Father’s place and utterly, completely defeat this chef through cooking.”
“How unusual of you, Motoyasu-san, to solve something with anything other than brute force… What’s brought this on?”
“Extermination isn’t the only thing I’m about, I say. This is my chance to properly show off my competence.”
“Ah… scoring points, I see. But Motoyasu-san, can you really manage something as sane as not slaughtering your opponent?”
What are you saying? This Motoyasu has not the slightest intention of falling behind anyone except Father.
“Motoyasu-san certainly seems highly motivated, but is he actually able to stand in for Naofumi-san?”
“Ah, yes… I do think it’s possible, but just how good is the Spear Hero-sama’s cooking, exactly?”

“Well, let’s see… There have been occasions when Motoyasu-san cooks for the Filolials in the village, so I have tasted it. Not on Naofumi-san’s level, but… I’d say he’s genuinely the second-best cook among us, after Naofumi-san.”

Itsuki explained my culinary skill to the envoy from the Dark Culinary World. I may not match Father, but I can cook too, I say. Not only did I cook for myself, but back in the day… I made all sorts of things for the pigs.
“I made shops so prosperous that lines formed at cultural festivals across various schools! And with the added bonus of weapon buffs, there’s no one to fear except Father, I say!”
“Bringing up cultural festivals as your example is very on-brand for you, Motoyasu-san…”
“Also, brace yourself and be amazed, I say. Father once entrusted me with the preparation of an extremely important dish, I say.”
After a moment’s thought at my words, Itsuki asked.
“Specifically, what kind of preparation? And which Naofumi-san was this?”
“The Father of the first world, I say. That Father entrusted me with processing the staple food.”
“Staple food… bread, noodles, potatoes? You do like potato dishes, Motoyasu-san.”
“Rice, I say. Father asked me to remove the broken grains and select, one by one, only the grains of uniform size, so I did that continuously.”
“Rice… wait, what? That means sorting by size, right? I feel like I’ve heard something like that in a manga somewhere, but… Naofumi-san, what on earth did you have Motoyasu-san do…”
What was it? Itsuki seemed to be at a loss for words for some reason. Whatever could be the matter?
“I’m impressed you carried it out without a single doubt. That you managed such an absurd task… That Naofumi-san really understood how to handle Motoyasu-san, didn’t he.”
“Filo-tan gave it her seal of approval, saying ’The rice has such a nice texture today!’ and I was so happy, I say.”
“Ah, so it actually had an effect… He didn’t just mix it all back together afterward to render it meaningless, then.”
Itsuki was saying something rather rude, I say. There’s no way Father would do something so pointless as digging a hole just to fill it back in for no reason.
“Well, if that works for you, then I suppose that’s fine…”
“Itsuki-kun, Itsuki-kun.”
Raph-emon, who had been silently listening the whole time, tugged at Itsuki’s hand to assert herself. Raph-emon seemed to have produced an apron from somewhere.
“The Lovey-Dovey Wife Apron! No matter how untalented you are, once you put on this apron, its power lets you cook any dish imaginable!”
